We asked for your thoughts after Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie between Sunderland and Brentford .
Ian: 11 changes proves how far this team have come in the past two seasons. I liked the look of the team before kick-off and boy did those young guys run for the club. Ta Bi and Talbi gave the team an out when under pressure and must be in serious contention for the rest of the season. Well done.
Tony: With 11 changes from Sunday and against another Premier League side, we did extremely well, especially in the first half. Not surprisingly a bit weary as the game went on, but a result the players can be proud of.
David: Lots of positives for the club on the night. Most of the stand-ins did themselves no harm at all, but Ahoka and Ta Bi caught the eye. It was good to see some pace and trickery going forward and Regis le Bris will have learned a lot and been given a lot of food for thought. Great to see the ownership on the pitch at the end.
Harry: Where have you been Mr Ta Bi? What a performance. Should be starting playing like that. All-round decent performance from the team and nice to see Fofana get his first goal. Brentford had a lot of quality on show so I'm very happy.
Nicholas: A long way to travel for a very poor performance. Problem is most people look at the league table and think everything is OK. Massive game against Nottingham Forest on Saturday. This was a massive missed opportunity.
Stephen: Yet another poor performance in the cup. We never seem to be able to play as a team on these occasions - too many poor individual performances. Sad to say but we did not deserve to win. I hope we can learn from this performance and push on.
Paul: Another very poor display and beaten by a Sunderland reserve side. Please don't tell me we were up for that game because it was embarrassing and something doesn't seem quite right with Bees at the moment - their attitude stinks.
Rob: I've said it once and I'll say it again, we play our best football in a 4-3-3. When is Keith Andrews going to realise this? It's clear that the double pivot in midfield does not work as the full-backs push forward too much and the wide players do not tuck in and run back to support. Get a grip, man, or get a new job before we end up in the bottom three.
